title: Cheap parts, poor design, incomplete operating instructions, and poor manufacturer support
text:
While the feeder has few parts, the lack of complete instructions makes construction harder than it should be. Cheap parts (plastic push pins to hold the feed chute in place and a very thin lid) further degrade this product. The display had no on or off button nor did it have a defined slot/space to securely hold the 6-volt battery. The Moultrie solar panel was provided with one 3/4" screw which was too short to secure it firmly to the feeder. The wires from the solar panel to the battery were not protected from varmints with either a sheath or covering. Instructions were not provided how to maximize battery life or how long a battery would last before it needed recharging. The display showed that the battery was fully charged yet would not work/remained blank despite repeated efforts to set the time, date, feeding times, etc. I guessed there should be a reset button somewhere and found it on the back of the display inside the battery compartment. I pressed it for 15 seconds or so and the display began working correctly. The printed instructions did not mention there was a reset button or how to use it.

Update One - the feeder quit spreading/dispensing deer corn after three weeks of use. The feed outlet was not jammed and corn dispensed freely when I hand whirled the metal dispenser. The display turned blank when the set time came to spread the corn. Pressing the reset button many times and changing the battery did not resolve the issue. I called Moultrie support. After a very long wait time, I told the representative what the problem was and what I'd done to try and resolve the issue. I was told they would send me a return label so I could return the unit to them for repair. I said deer season is three weeks from now and I won't be able to use the feeder this year if I send in the broken dispenser. The representative said she was sorry but turnaround was fast, usually a week and a half or so. She also said that they could not send a replacement dispenser. This is a bunch of crap - if I send in my broken dispenser, why not send me a replacement as soon as they see my broken unit is on the way back to them? Now I have feeder that's broken and the issue can't be resolved so it can be used by the time deer season starts.

Update Two - the promised return label was never emailed to me. After a week of waiting, I called Moultrie back and explained that I had a defective feeder and was told I would be emailed a return label which I never received. I was told the previous agent hadn't written my email address so the form was never sent. The new agent said she didn't have the authority to send me the return label and would transfer me to a "higher up" who would resolve my issue. After 30 minutes of waiting and no response I hung up and initiated a support chat on the Moultrie web site. The support chat representative told me the other two Moultrie agents were wrong and the customer is responsible (pays) for sending a defective unit to Moultrie. She directed me to another web page where I was told to fill out a warranty return form and submit it electronically. I was also told to print the completed form out and include it in the box with the defective unit. The form printed out on three pages - the first page page was blank, the second page had my contact information, and the third page did not include the description of the problem I had included with the just submitted electronic form. I hand wrote out the description of the problem and attached it to the other forms including the proof of purchase. The dispenser cost $19+ to send to Moultrie's repair shop via the US Post Office.

This has been the worst support service and warranty return process I have ever encountered. Moultrie obviously discourages any repairs or returns despite glowing language about their customer service on their web site. Further, if I'd known how poorly designed and constructed this feeder was I would have never ordered it. Saying that - I'm past the point where it can be returned to Amazon for a refund. I will never purchase another Moultrie product and will tell all my friends that are thinking of buying one of their products of my experiences and advise them not to.

title: Sadly dissapointed.
text:
I really wanted to love this tricycle. I have severely broken both of my legs a couple of years apart. Needless to say, I have developed a fear of falling and re-injuring either leg. Rather than take a chance riding a two wheel bike, I chose a tricycle so I could ride with my family. Pro's: I can't think of any. Con's: The directions and video were ambiguous and skipped crucial steps when building the bike. It took a few hours to completely assemble between my husband and myself. After assembling, we took it outside for a trial run. The bike chain was too lose, so we adjusted it by one segment. Then the chain was extraordinarily tight. We attempted to adjust the bike multiple time within the two weeks it was put together with no luck. Then, as you can see in the pictures above, the fan shaped piece that attaches the fenders to the bike broke off. Upon closer inspection, it appears to have had a very poor weld. That was the last straw for me. Even if we had figured out the problem with the chain, there is no way I was keeping a bike that I paid $350 for when pieces were already breaking off.
We did not keep the original packaging, so I purchased an extra-large wardrobe box, bubble wrap, and tape and packed it up. It is so poorly made that I am fortunately still within the return window. I'm out about $40 to pack it but that is a small price to pay to get the majority of my money back. I would not purchase this bike or any similar to it again.

title: Not a Xootr, but pretty good
text:
I ordered this for my kiddo. I own an original Xootr from the first year of production, and it's still going strong, so that's my basis for comparison.

CONs:
* Rattly from brand new. The pins that fit into the front recepticles after unfolding and lock it in riding position are slack in the slots, meaning they rattle and that makes the whole steering move. It feels like the headset is loose. (I checked, it's not.) I'll probably fill those with a pair of custom plastic bushing made from insta-morph plastic.
*I'm 6'3", and this razor won't fit me comfortably. Sure, I could make it work, but the Xootr is a better fit.
*Separable bars: I like the (fixed) handlebars better on the xootr than the disconnecting ones on the razors. They don't add that much to the folded dimensions, and they don't dangle from cheap bungie, as the Razor's bars do.
*Still that little, narrow deck. I like a bigger deck, but hey, with a few screws and a piece of ply or carbon fiber panel, this would be a simple mod.

PRO:
* Nice big rear fender. That rear brake keeps street crud off the back of your legs. City street slime is gross, and the trails by us have all sorts of animal crap you'd rather not be wearing.
* Nice front fender too!
*The wheels on the razor are actually bigger than the Xootr, which is saying something. Big wheels are important. Before the Xootr, I tried commuting on the then-popular regular razor, and those little wheels were death on cracks or pavement irregularities. Bigger wheels deal much better.
* 1/3 the price of the Xootr.
label: positive

title: IronBull?  More like IronBS
text:
I bought these to experiment with new equipment/straps and as an inexpensive alternative to the 2 sets of Versa Grips which I have owned. I was quite satisfied with my Versa Grips and each pair lasted about two years (training 3-5 times a week) before ripping. These "IronBull" grips literally lasted through 7 workouts. I wish I had taken a picture of the end result after my last workout because the left hand strap had ripped entirely through the neoprene center. I was hanging from my pull-up bar only by my finger tips and the fabric edges. Had the fabric torn as well, it was entirely possible I would have dislocated my right shoulder (of the one strap which had not torn).
7 workouts Really? I need my money back.
Please go with Versa Grips they are worth the extra money.
label: negative

title: Warning! May increase SI joint pain
text: A physician friend recommended The Plane to me as a way of strengthening leg and core muscles, and, hopefully, reducing my lower back pain.  I did exactly as the instructions said -- starting slowly and working up. I used the board at work and at home for a week. My back pain steadily increased with usage to the point where I had to stop.  The idea is great. Just know this is not a magic cure for chronic lower back pain (mine is SI joint).  I returned the board. Although it took a full week after the company received the board back for them to issue a refund, they did stand behind their guarantee.
label: neutral
